text:
Priya: Hey all — starting my first on-call shadow shift next Tue-Thu and wanted to sync on the pairing plan and any gaps to watch for. I'm available for a 30m walk-through before I take the first shadow shift.

Aisha: welcome! :tada: i'm primary for Tue morning, can pair at 10am PT on Tuesday. will show the routing rules and our triage checklist.

Marco: I'm secondary Tue/Wed nights. Priya — if you want I can run the DB failover run in the staging sandbox so you can watch. Takes ~20m.

Priya: yes please — sandbox run would be great. what's the best slot?

Aisha: let's do Tue 10am PT for the overview and Wed 9am PT for the sandbox failover.

Tom: Quick note on coverage gaps: we have only one engineer oncall for Fri-Sun next month (vacations), so if anything critical happens during that weekend we'll need escalation rules tightened. I'll follow up with schedule.

Priya: noted. would love to see the weekend escalation policy.

Aisha: here's the lightweight handoff checklist we follow — copy/paste into your notes: 
```
- Confirm primary/secondary for next 24h
- Check dashboard for model-serving error spikes
- Verify any ongoing incidents in #incidents
- Validate last deploys and rollback flags
- Ensure runbook links available & test alert routes
```

Marco: also add: validate `kv-cache` warming job status — it's a common perf hit after deploys.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-9072 — high 95th pct latency on hosted text-gen pool (region-us-west). Pager escalated to on-call primary. https://incidents.redwood/INC-9072

Priya: oh nice, can we walk through that incident flow during the pairing so I can see a live example?

Aisha: absolutely — we'll do the triage run now. Marco, can you pull recent logs?

Marco: pulling: `kubectl logs -n inference svc/text-gen-frontend --since=15m` — seeing repeated `KV_MISS` spikes and some gRPC 14 (unavailable) from a subset of nodes.

Tom: probable cause: a recent config tweak changed the batching window for that pool. If the window is too small, it increases per-token overhead. Paging rule threshold triggers at 95th > 450ms for 5 minutes.

Aisha: ok let's follow runbook section "High latency - text-gen" https://redwood.internal/runbooks/oncall-textgen#high-latency — TL;DR steps: check pool health, confirm kernel mismatch, fallback to older model variant, and open rollback if needed.

SRE-Runbook-Bot: Runbook snippet pulled: "If 95th latency > 450ms for >5m: (1) Check pool nodes: `rctl pool status text-gen-usw` (2) If nodes show OOM/503, route to variant `text-gen-v1.9` (3) Notify infra and start canary rollback."

Priya: cool. during the sandbox we'll do steps 1-3?

Marco: yes — sandbox failover will include routing to `text-gen-v1.9` and validating responses. I'll prepare a safe rollback script: `scripts/route-fallback.sh --pool=text-gen-usw --variant=text-gen-v1.9`

Aisha: and a reminder about customer impact classification: for hosted API we mark "P2 - degraded latency" unless errors exceed 5% or there's data loss, then escalate to P1. We log the customer-visible note in the incident ticket.

Priya: who handles customer comms when I'm shadowing? should I draft notes or just observe?

Tom: observe first. after a couple shadows you'll draft the initial note and we'll review before posting.

Aisha: covering shift swaps: if you need to swap primary, use the oncall rota page and ping `#eng-oncall` with the swap message. Template: `Swap: Aisha -> Priya on 2026-05-12 10:00-18:00 PT reason: personal`. We try to avoid last-minute swaps during release windows.

Marco: added prep exercise: Priya, before Wed sandbox, try this command in staging to see the pool status: `rctl pool status text-gen-usw --json | jq '.nodes[] | {name,.status}'` — it prints node health.

Priya: got it. one more Q: where do I find the paging thresholds per pool?

Aisha: dashboards -> Observability -> Model Pools -> select pool -> Alerts tab. Also we keep a short mapping in the runbook index: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/pool-alerts.md

oncall-bot: Reminder: On-call orientation checklist overdue for Priya (2 items). Run `oncall-bot checklist show priya` to view.

Priya: running now... `oncall-bot checklist show priya` shows: 1) Verify Slack pager routing 2) Complete sandbox failover exercise.

Tom: ping me if you hit an auth error during sandbox; there was an API key rotation last month that can block older tokens.

Aisha: final: we'll do a live handoff script on Thursday morning at 9:55am PT where current primary posts the Handoff message in thread and confirms `primary` updated in rota. Example handoff post: `Handoff: Aisha -> Marco 2026-05-14 10:00 PT. No active incidents. Verified dashboards.`

Priya: thanks all — this is super helpful. See you Tue 10am PT. I'll join with my laptop and notes.

Marco: welcome aboard :raised_hands: — we try to keep things low-stress, ask lots of questions.

Aisha: see you. I'll DM a calendar invite for the pairing + the sandbox run.

oncall-bot: Handoff template saved to `/runbooks/handoffs/handoff-template.md`.

Priya: closing note: can someone point me to the list of common mitigation commands? would be great to copy into my quick reference.

Aisha: here's a short list to save: `rctl pool status`, `kubectl logs -n inference`, `scripts/route-fallback.sh`, `rctl cache warm --pool=...`, `pg-rotate-read-replicas --cluster=...` — we'll add to your onboarding doc.

Tom: putting the weekend coverage concern on my calendar to propose a rotation change by EOD Friday.

Priya: awesome, thanks team!
